caption: An interface names the shape a value must have — every property, and its type.
A ? marks a property optional. readonly allows reading freely but blocks reassignment after creation.

eyebrow: type does the same job, differently
caption: type aliases can name an object shape too — but also a primitive, or a union of specific string values, which interfaces can't do.

eyebrow: Declaration merging — interface's one real edge
caption: Declaring the same interface twice merges its members. Doing the same with type is a compiler error.
